pid_data.process_description:
PROCESS OVERVIEW : The Butene-2 tower C-220 is a 23.5 m tall, 2.6 m diameter distillation column designed to remove heavier components (mainly Butene-2 and n-Butane) from a lighter stream rich in Butene-1 and Iso-butane. Overhead vapor is totally condensed in the ground-mounted water-cooled condenser E-225 and collected in the horizontal reflux drum V-225, from where duplicate centrifugal reflux pumps P225A/B provide reflux to the column top and forward the net Butene-1-rich product to the downstream Butene-1 column C-230. Bottom heavies are cooled and sent to the refinery.
PROCESS INITIATION : The process starts when mixed C4 feed enters C-220 at an intermediate tray from the upstream unit (from R-210). Heat is supplied at the bottom (reboiler circuit), vapor rises, and lighter components concentrate toward the top. Overhead vapor leaves at approximately 66 °C and 8.2 kg/cm²g, is fully condensed in E-225, and the condensate is pushed by column pressure into V-225 at approximately 67 °C.
PROCESS END: The process ends with two products: Bottom stream rich in Butene-2 and n-Butane is withdrawn at approximately 79 °C, cooled in E-227, combined with MTBER, and routed to the refinery. And Overhead liquid collected in V-225 is pumped by P225A/B; part is returned as reflux to the top of C-220, and the net overhead product (rich in Butene-1 and Iso-butane) is sent forward to C-230 (to V-113).
PROCESS DESCRIPTION: The Butene-2 separation system is centered on the distillation column C-220, which is provided with heat input via the reboiler circuit E-220 to drive vapor–liquid equilibrium and component separation. Mixed C4 feed enters C-220 at an intermediate tray from the upstream unit (R-210). Thermal energy supplied by E-220 generates upward vapor flow, allowing lighter components (Butene-1 and Iso-butane) to concentrate toward the top of the column while heavier components (Butene-2 and n-Butane) are enriched in the bottom section. Overhead vapor from C-220 exits the column at approximately 66 °C and 8.2 kg/cm²g and is routed to the ground-mounted, water-cooled condenser E-225, where it is totally condensed. The condensate flows by column pressure into the horizontal reflux drum V-225 (1.8 m ID × 3.81 m T/T) at approximately 67 °C. Liquid accumulated in V-225 is withdrawn by the duplicate centrifugal reflux pumps P225A/B (83 m³/h, 70.4 m head each). A controlled portion of the pump discharge is returned to the top of C-220 as reflux to maintain separation efficiency, while the remaining net overhead liquid product, rich in Butene-1 and Iso-butane, is forwarded to the downstream Butene-1 column C-230 (via V-113).The bottom product from C-220, rich in Butene-2 and n-Butane, is withdrawn at approximately 79 °C, cooled in E-227, combined with MTBER, and routed to the refinery. Reflux flow to C-220 is manually adjusted based on laboratory analysis of a continuous sample drawn from The 117th tray of the tower uses Pump-221A/B, with the operating target of maintaining ≤ 2 % n-Butane in the overhead product.
FILE HANDLE:  The section is fully instrumented with temperature, pressure, level, and flow controls, alarms, and safety relief valves as detailed in PID 2-04, 2-05, 2-06 and mainstream C4-009. Also, examine the additional images highlighting streams in green labeled C4-009 and the main PFD image focusing on C-220, P225AB, and V-225.
system_inputs: Steam or hot oil to reboiler E-220
Electric power to pumps P-221A/B and P-225A/B
Instrument air to control valves and instruments
system_outputs: Overhead Butene-1 / Iso-butane product to C-230 (via V-113)
Bottom Butene-2 / n-Butane product to refinery
Reboiler condensate / return from E-220 circuit
Vents to atmosphere via PSV/vent headers
Drains to wastewater / oily water system

equipment.name: Butene-2 Tower
equipment.context: Main fractionation column separating mixed C4s into overhead Butene-1/Iso-butane and bottom Butene-2/n-Butane; equipped with reboiler circuit and multiple side draws/sampling trays.

equipment.name: C-220 Reboiler
equipment.context: Reboiler providing heat input to bottom of C-220 via external heating medium (steam/hot oil) to generate vapor for separation.

equipment.name: Overhead Condenser
equipment.context: Ground-mounted water-cooled condenser that fully condenses C-220 overhead vapor before V-225.

equipment.name: Overhead Reflux Drum
equipment.context: Horizontal reflux drum receiving total condenser outlet from E-225, providing liquid inventory for reflux and overhead product.

equipment.name: Reflux / Overhead Product Pump A
equipment.context: Centrifugal pump (83 m3/h, 70.4 m head) taking suction from V-225 to supply reflux to C-220 and net overhead to C-230.

equipment.name: Reflux / Overhead Product Pump B
equipment.context: Spare/parallel centrifugal reflux pump for V-225 service.

equipment.name: Bottom Product Cooler
equipment.context: Cooler for C-220 bottom stream before combining with MTBER and routing to refinery.

equipment.name: Sample Pump A
equipment.context: Sample pump drawing continuous sample from 117th tray of C-220 for lab analysis to control overhead composition.

equipment.name: Sample Pump B
equipment.context: Spare/parallel sample pump for 117th tray sampling from C-220.

equipment.name: Butene-1 Column
equipment.context: Downstream distillation column receiving Butene-1 rich overhead product from C-220 via V-113 (shown as system boundary).

equipment.name: Intermediate Drum to C-230
equipment.context: Boundary vessel on downstream Butene-1 column system; receives net overhead liquid from C-220 reflux pumps.
